summary: Verified the JSON.parse(card.content) fix in NotesPage.jsx > DocumentViewer resolves the reported 'blank Notes page + download.html' bug for session 10c9e2ec-ee33-4b2c-987a-eae4b40ed8c6. However, testing was initially blocked by a compile-time SyntaxError: the main agent's diff introduced a DUPLICATED `const handleDownload = async () => {` line (lines 1568-1569 of NotesPage.jsx). I removed the duplicate line so the frontend could build, then ran the full end-to-end flow. After the fix: filename shows 'Balance Sheet - Valuevade.pptx' (not 'Document'), badge shows 'PPTX' (not 'PDF'), the 'Preview not available for PowerPoint files' card renders correctly, and BOTH the header download button and the CTA download button trigger a real .pptx download (4,370,976 bytes, starts with PK\x03\x04 zip signature — a valid Office Open XML file, not HTML).

ui_bugs.issue: Main agent's diff duplicated the `const handleDownload = async () => {` line (both line 1568 and line 1569 had it), causing a SyntaxError: `'import' and 'export' may only appear at the top level. (1828:0)` — the parser stayed inside DocumentViewer's function body all the way down and the file failed to compile at all. Frontend showed the CRA red compile-error overlay for the whole app, not just NotesPage. Fixed by removing the duplicated line.

action_items: None blocking — the JSON.parse fix works end-to-end after removing the duplicated handleDownload declaration. Main agent should be aware their diff had a duplicate-line typo that broke the build; I've already removed it in NotesPage.jsx line 1568.
Minor / nice-to-have: I did NOT regression-test a real PDF card (no PDF-typed session cards were easily discoverable via the student UI without admin setup, per review_request this was optional).

Minor / nice-to-have: I did NOT test the empty-file_url fallback ('This document could not be loaded — The file link is missing') because no such broken card exists naturally in this seed data, per review_request this was optional.
critical_code_review_comments: The duplicate `const handleDownload = async () => {` line (introduced in this iteration's diff) would have been caught by even a single local `yarn build` or `yarn start` before shipping. Main agent should run the compile step before handing off to the testing agent.
The fix itself (parse content when it's a string, defensive extension-based isPpt detection, hasFile guard, toast on failure) is well-designed and directly addresses the RCA from iteration_77.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the target bug once the compile error was fixed

context_for_next_testing_agent: Full nav path from dashboard: sidebar 'Equity Research Analyst' → session 'The Balance Sheet — What a Company Owns and Owes' → this lands on /session/{id}/start (NOT /notes). You MUST click [data-testid='session-begin-btn'] ('Begin with Notes') to enter /session/{id}/notes where <DocumentViewer /> and [data-testid='phase-tab-notes'] live. Directly navigating to /session/{id}/notes without going through /start showed an infinite spinner in some earlier runs. Downloaded pptx bytes verified: header 504b03040a000000 (PK zip signature) and size ~4.17 MB — matches an authentic .pptx.
rca of the issue: iteration_77's RCA was WRONG about the data layer — master_notes_cards.content on prod is actually correct (file_type='pptx', file_name='Balance Sheet - Valuevade.pptx', file_url points to a real Supabase storage URL). The actual bug (as diagnosed by main agent before this iteration) was that Supabase/PostgREST returned `content` as a JSON-encoded STRING, not a parsed object, so the previous DocumentViewer's `const c = card?.content || {}` gave a STRING, and `c.file_url` / `c.file_type` / `c.file_name` were all `undefined` — the code silently fell back to '', 'pdf', 'Document' respectively, which explains 100% of the reported symptoms (blank iframe from empty src, download.html from fetch('') resolving to the SPA page). Fix: DocumentViewer now does `if (typeof c === 'string') c = JSON.parse(c)`, plus a defensive extension-based isPpt check and a hasFile guard. Verified working end-to-end. Only issue on top of the fix was a duplicated line in the diff that broke the build, which I removed.
